title: Gravity as Computation Time: A Local Budget Rule on a Spin-1/2 Phase-Bit Lattice and its Post-Newtonian Limit
description:
We ask whether gravity can be modelled as a local limit on how fast each node of a discrete quantum lattice can compute. The test particle is a unitary quantum walker on the face-centred-cubic lattice whose spin is carried by a finite register, the binary octahedral group 2O: every 60° turn rotates the spinor by a quarter turn about a cube axis. This gives spin 1/2 with Kramers degeneracy at every momentum, the belt-trick sign, and exact particle–antiparticle symmetry; a single extra amplitude, “reverse the heading without rotating the spin”, is the lattice Dirac mass (gap exactly 4μ).

Slowing down only the internal clock gives Nordström gravity; a local wait buffer per node gives Einstein's 1911 theory (half light bending). A single node rule — every process needs each node it involves to be free, one node for the clock and two for a hop — produces H = N2K + NM, i.e. a spatial metric A = 1/N and γPPN = 1. Combining loads at a node as independent occupations (N = ∏ Ni) gives βPPN = 1 even in the strong field, and a direction-independent drag hop supplies g0i with the coefficient the relativity principle demands. In the full 3+1D walker light is deflected 2.07 times more strongly than with waiting alone (GR: 2), the classical orbits of the lattice metric give the general-relativistic perihelion advance, and a lattice gravitational atom reproduces the fine structure ∝ 2γ+1 (de Sitter) and the Lense–Thirring hyperfine shifts of the Dirac equation in the corresponding metric to 1–4%. The field equations for lapse and shift, a vacuum counterterm and the gyroscope rule are imposed and stated as such; the tensor sector (gravitational waves) is the decisive open question.

The paper (LaTeX and PDF) is in papers/paper3_gravity_computation_time.*; the repository also contains all simulation code, stored data and the result documents behind every number.
